rv.q: These elements have been combined, with alchemical magic, into the theatrical equivalent of comfort food.

“Mamma Mia!,” which weaves a few threads of romantic comedy around a bumper crop of old Abba tunes, is a thoroughly preposterous show, but it’s also a giddy guilty pleasure, and its arrival on Broadway in a time of unforeseen anxiety has an aura of sweet inevitability.
The Broadway production maintains the sweetness, and that’s a joy.
As theater, Mamma Mia! is forgettable.
“Mamma Mia!” flies as tuneful as a lark and as smart as a cuckoo.

Now, they'll get the chance to do just that as the musical returns to its original home — the Theatre — for a six-month-long limited engagement that may not reinvent the material, but is still every bit the dreamy, endlessly endearing experience that fans know and love.

As triumphantly calculating as Andersson and Ulvaeus were in formulating their songs, that's how triumphantly calculating the Mamma Mia! producers have been in crating a money machine that doesn't need critical acclaim.

"In terms of theatre, Mamma Mia! has little to offer. The book is paper thin, silly...Still, the legions of ABBA fans who attend Mamma Mia! aren't going to care about much of this. They will doubtlessly have a great time and may well walk away proclaiming Mamma Mia! one of the best shows they've ever seen.
Mamma Mia! revels primarily in its own construction, it's manufactured rather than inspired and so is much of what passes for fun in the show.
Personally, I left this theater ready to get my groove on!
The bristling misogyny of The Women is unsettling, whether it resides in the characters or in the author.
The cast as a whole is uniformly terrific, spot on full of zing, broad smiles and what appears to be true joy.

tn.cat: Best Featured Actress in a Musical

cn.t: Critics find this ABBA jukebox musical light on substance but irresistibly fun, with infectious energy and joy that overshadow its flimsy plot and manufactured feel.

vs.sum: The Winter Garden Theatre offers excellent legroom and spacious seating, making it one of the most comfortable venues on Broadway. Sightlines are generally good, though some side seats may have partial obstructions. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historical charm and garden-themed decor, while facilities are average with some potential for lines at restrooms.

acc.note: 20 wheelchair spaces (largest of Shubert theaters). 16 aisle transfer seats. Infrared devices available.
